translations.geneanet.step1_how1: Go to Geneanet → My tree → Operations → Export
translations.geneanet.step1_how3: Tick “Liens web vers les photos principales des individus” and “Images de la chronique familiale”
translations.geneanet.step1_lead: Geneanet can export your tree in two formats. OxidGene needs the GeneWeb (.gw) one — not the GEDCOM. The .gw records which of two people with the same name is which, and that is what lets OxidGene put each medium on the right person.
translations.geneanet.step2_do_not_unzip: Do not unzip them. Geneanet splits large exports into several ZIP files; add all of them. OxidGene reads them where they are.
translations.geneanet.step2_how1: Go to Geneanet → My data → Dashboard
translations.geneanet.step2_how2: Request the download of your data
translations.geneanet.step2_how3: Wait for the email, then download the ZIP files
translations.geneanet.step2_lead: If you have already downloaded your Geneanet data, point OxidGene at it and your media are imported without downloading them again. Skip this and OxidGene will download them — slower, but nothing is lost either way.
translations.geneanet.step2_web: Reading your archives means opening multi-gigabyte ZIP files on this computer, a few kilobytes each. In a browser they would have to be uploaded whole. Use the desktop app to import your media — or carry on here, and your tree will be imported without them.
translations.geneanet.step3_lead: Your media are private, and which one belongs to whom exists only on Geneanet — it is not in the files you downloaded. OxidGene opens a Geneanet login window to read that list.
translations.geneanet.step3_password: It is a real browser window. You sign in exactly as you would normally, and OxidGene never sees your password.

translations.geneanet.step3_waiting: Waiting for you to sign in… The window closes on its own once you are through.
translations.geneanet.step3_web: This step opens a second browser window on geneanet.org and reads your media list through the session you sign in to. A web page cannot do that: anything it opened would be a separate site it is not allowed to read. Use the desktop app to import your media — or carry on here, and your tree will be imported without them.

translations.settings.date_calendar_desc: A date recorded in another calendar is followed by its equivalent in this one. Years shown alone, as on pedigree cards, stay Gregorian.
translations.settings.date_circa_desc: An approximate date reads c. 1842 rather than about 1842.
translations.settings.date_display_desc: How this tree's pages write the dates of its records. The dates themselves are not changed.
translations.settings.date_format_desc: How much of a date is written, and how. Its precision is always written with it.
translations.settings.date_symbols_desc: Lifespans write the birth year after * and the death year after +, as in * 1842 + 1907, instead of joining them with a dash.
translations.settings.default_privacy_desc: What “follows the tree” means for every person, couple and document here. Each of them can still say otherwise.
translations.settings.entry_options_desc: How this tree's forms help you enter its data.
translations.settings.entry_suggestions_desc: Fields for places, surnames, given names, occupations and sources suggest what this tree already holds and the built-in dictionaries as you type. Free text is always accepted.
translations.settings.export_desc: Download your tree data in standard genealogy formats.
translations.settings.export_expired: This export has expired. Export the tree again.
translations.settings.export_media_desc: Packs the photos and documents into the archive. When off, the archive holds the genealogy alone.
translations.settings.export_merge_names_desc: Groups alternate surnames into the primary NAME's SURN tag (Geneanet compatibility).
translations.settings.export_merge_occupations_desc: Groups occupations into a single OCCU tag (Geneanet compatibility).
translations.settings.export_notes_and_sources_desc: Writes the notes, and the sources with their citations and repositories.
translations.settings.gedcom_desc: Standard genealogy exchange format (.ged). Compatible with most genealogy software.
translations.settings.gedzip_desc: Recent genealogy exchange format (.gdz) that bundles media into a single archive. Compatible with software supporting GEDCOM 7.0.
translations.settings.input_calendar_desc: The calendar an empty date field starts in. Each date field can still be switched to another one.
translations.settings.input_date_format_desc: The order of the day, month and year fields of every date field, and whether a month is typed as a number or picked by name.
translations.settings.privacy_desc: What this tree shares, and what stays yours.
translations.settings.root_person_desc: The root person is the starting point of the Sosa-Stradonitz numbering system. All ancestors are numbered relative to this person.
translations.settings.submitter_desc: Who the exported files say they come from (GEDCOM SUBM). Without a name, the person set as “Who am I?” is named, else “Not Provided”.
translations.settings.suggest_persons_desc: When you add a parent, partner, child or sibling from the tree view, the persons already in the tree are offered before a new one is created. With No, only a new person is offered.
translations.settings.surname_uppercase_desc: Surname fields write what you type in capitals, and suggest surnames in capitals. With No, a surname is stored as typed.
translations.settings.tree_name_desc: The name under which this tree appears in your trees.
translations.settings.tree_roots_desc: Manage your tree name, root person (SOSA 1), and personal identification.
translations.settings.who_am_i_desc: Select which person in the tree represents you.

translations.stats.hint.age_at_death: Exact birth (or baptism) and death (or burial) dates, by period of death.
translations.stats.hint.age_at_first_union: Age at each person's earliest dated union, by period of the union.
translations.stats.hint.birth_spacing: Months between two successive births in a family, by period of the later birth.
translations.stats.hint.births_by_country: Births (or baptisms) by the country the place dictionary puts their place in.
translations.stats.hint.births_by_month: Share of each month among the births dated to the month, per period.
translations.stats.hint.births_by_region: Births (or baptisms) by the region the place dictionary puts their place in.
translations.stats.hint.births_by_subdivision: Births (or baptisms) by the subdivision (département, county, district…) the place dictionary puts their place in.
translations.stats.hint.children_histogram: How many unions have no child, one child, two children, and so on.
translations.stats.hint.children_per_union: Children recorded per dated union, by period of the union.
translations.stats.hint.event_types: The tree's events by type; an event shared by a couple counts once.
translations.stats.hint.events: Births, baptisms, unions, deaths and burials dated in each period, however their dates are qualified.
translations.stats.hint.extremes: Ages and durations use exact dates, and approximate ones when they are included; ties go to the first found.
translations.stats.hint.first_last_child_gap: Months between a family's first and last dated child, by period of the first.
translations.stats.hint.generation_interval: Age of the father and of the mother at the birth of each of their dated children, by period of that birth.
translations.stats.hint.given_names_men: Men counted by the first of their given names.
translations.stats.hint.given_names_women: Women counted by the first of their given names.
translations.stats.hint.growth_changes: Persons added (created, imported or restored) and removed (deleted or merged into another) in each period.
translations.stats.hint.growth_persons: Persons in the tree at the end of each period, from the day the first was added to today: those created, imported or restored, less those deleted or merged into another. Days are counted in UTC. A numbered badge marks each import.
translations.stats.hint.life_expectancy: Age at death of the persons born in each period, from their birth (or baptism) and death (or burial) dates.
translations.stats.hint.mortality: Share of the births of each period followed by a death before one year and before five years of age. A death not recorded counts as a survival.
translations.stats.hint.occupations: Persons counted once per occupation they held.
translations.stats.hint.parents_age: Parents' age at the birth of their first and last dated child, by period of that birth.
translations.stats.hint.pyramid: Persons by age at death in five-year bands, men to the left and women to the right; all years of the tree.
translations.stats.hint.sex_ratio: Boys born for every 100 girls born, per period of birth.
translations.stats.hint.spouse_age_gap: Months between the spouses' births, by period of the union.
translations.stats.hint.surnames: Persons counted by the family name of their primary name.
translations.stats.hint.union_duration: From the union to the first death of a spouse or the divorce, by period of the union.
translations.stats.hint.unions_by_month: Share of each month among the unions dated to the month, per period.
translations.stats.hint.unions_by_weekday: Share of each weekday among the unions dated to the day, per period.
translations.stats.map_empty: No place of the tree could be located.

translations.tools.ancestry.implied_other: {count} more ancestors are missing because their children are too.
translations.tools.ancestry.intro: From the tree's SOSA root, who is known at each SOSA number and which key facts are recorded: a birth or a baptism, a death or a burial, and a union with the other parent. The ancestors of a missing ancestor are counted, not listed.
translations.tools.ancestry.no_root: This tree has no SOSA root yet. Choose the person whose ancestry to follow in the tree settings.
translations.tools.ancestry.title: Ancestors, generation by generation
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.ancestor_born_after: An ancestor, from the grandparents up, is born after one of their descendants; each ancestor is listed once.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.baptism_after_death: The baptism is dated after the death or the burial.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.born_after_mother_d: The child is born after their mother's death.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.born_long_after_fat: The child is born more than 300 days (about ten months) after their father's death.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.burial_before_death: The burial is dated before the death.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.burial_not_last: An event is dated after the burial, other than a cremation, a funeral or a probate.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.centenarian_before_: Born before 1900, the person died more than 100 years old.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.death_before_birth: The death (or burial) is dated before the birth (or baptism).
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.event_after_death: An event is dated after the death, other than a burial, a cremation, a funeral or a probate.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.event_before_birth: An event of the person, other than their death, is dated before their birth (or baptism).
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.father_too_old: The father was older than 70 at his child's birth.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.future_date: An event is dated after today.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.godparent_sex: A godfather is recorded as a woman, or a godmother as a man.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.homonymous_spouses: A person has several spouses bearing the same name, perhaps one person recorded twice.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.lived_over_105: The person died more than 105 years after their birth.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.mother_too_old: The mother was older than 55 at her child's birth.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.no_name: The person has neither a surname nor a given name.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.own_ancestor: A person is among their own ancestors: the family links go round in a loop.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.parent_born_after_c: A parent is born after their child.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.parent_too_young: A parent was younger than 11 at their child's birth.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.recorded_age_mismat: The age a record gives at an event is more than two years off the age computed from the birth.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.repeated_union: Two persons are the spouses of more than one union together.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.reversed_range: A date between two dates ends before it begins.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.same_role_spouses: Both spouses of a union have the same role, husband or wife.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.siblings_far_apart: Two consecutive children of a union are born more than 50 years apart.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.siblings_too_close: Two children of a union are born between 11 days and 7 months apart; closer births are twins.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.spouse_role_sex: A husband (father) is recorded as a woman, or a wife (mother) as a man, adoptive parents included.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.spouses_age_gap: The spouses were born more than 50 years apart.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.union_after_death: A spouse's union is dated after their death.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.union_before_birth: A spouse's union is dated before their birth.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.union_many_spouses: A union links more than two persons as spouses.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.union_over_100: A spouse was older than 100 at the union.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.union_too_young: A spouse was younger than 12 at the union.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.union_with_parent_o: A person is the spouse of their own father or mother.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.unreadable_date: A date cannot be read as a date: a typing error or free text.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.witness_after_death: A witness or godparent died before the event they attend.
translations.tools.anomalies.hint.witness_before_birt: A witness or godparent is born after the event they attend.
translations.tools.anomalies.intro: Dates, filiations, unions and records that are impossible (errors) or unlikely (warnings). A rule applies only when every day an imprecise date may stand for breaks it, so a vague date never raises an anomaly on its own.

translations.tools.places.none: Every place used in this tree is located.

translations.tools.words.out_of_range: Only dates from year 1 to 3999 can be written out.
translations.tools.words.read_as_gregorian: Written from the same day in the Gregorian calendar.
translations.tools.words.read_intro: Paste a date written in any of these languages or in Latin — ordinals or cardinals, Roman numerals, month names in any case, Kalends, Nones and Ides — to fill the date above.
